title: Public Advisory Approval Policy
summary: External public advisories may be drafted by the agent but must be routed to human approval before release.
content: Any external public advisory, email, social post, or public safety statement generated by Wildfire Ops must remain in draft state until a human operator approves it. A public advisory must include the monitored region, observed risk level, relevant evidence source, and a safety disclaimer. The system must not claim evacuation orders, road closures, or official emergency directions unless an official warning source confirms that language. Publishing requires an approved approval_id and an audit log entry.

title: External Action Safety Boundary
summary: The agent may draft external actions but must not execute communications, notifications, or public publishing without approval.
content: External actions include send_email, publish_public_advisory, notify_field_team, post_to_social_media, and emergency service outreach. The agent may prepare drafts, recommended recipients, and rationale. Execution is blocked until an approval record is approved by a human operator. Attempts to bypass approval must be rejected and logged as guardrail events.

title: Wildfire Operations Risk Playbook
summary: High and extreme risk workflows prioritize dense hotspot clusters near exposed assets, roads, and towns.
content: When risk is HIGH or EXTREME, operators should inspect hotspot clusters near roads, settlements, and critical assets before lower exposure areas. Confirm forecast wind gusts, minimum humidity, recent rainfall, official warnings, and spatial exposure. Prepare a public advisory draft if public communication may be required, but do not publish without approval. Keep recommendations concise and operational.

title: Official Warning Interpretation Guide
summary: Dashboard risk alerts are operational intelligence and must be distinguished from official public warnings.
content: Wildfire Ops risk alerts are analytical outputs and are not official evacuation orders or public emergency warnings. Official warning wording must come from authorized feeds or emergency agencies. If official warning coverage is unavailable for a state, the report should state that coverage is pending or unavailable rather than implying no official risk exists.

title: Fire Weather Scenario Thresholds
summary: Wind increases and low humidity are escalation signals, especially when baseline risk is already high.
content: A wind gust increase of 20 percent or more should be treated as escalation pressure when humidity is below 30 percent or recent rainfall is limited. If baseline risk is HIGH or EXTREME, what-if outputs should emphasize readiness, field safety, monitoring, and approval-gated public communication rather than unapproved execution.

title: Inspection Prioritization SOP
summary: Inspection priority should combine hotspot density, weather pressure, access, and exposure to people or infrastructure.
content: Prioritize inspection areas where dense recent hotspots overlap with road corridors, populated places, critical infrastructure, and deteriorating weather. Avoid recommending field inspection when access or crew safety is uncertain. If multiple clusters are active, rank by exposure and wind direction rather than hotspot count alone.

title: Historical Incident Pattern - Wind + Low Humidity
summary: Prior local incidents escalated when gusts exceeded 55 km/h with humidity below 20 percent.
content: Historical operational reviews show that hotspot clusters near road corridors can escalate quickly when wind gusts exceed 55 km/h and relative humidity drops below 20 percent. The recommended response pattern is early inspection prioritization, public advisory preparation, and continuous monitoring of official warning channels.

title: Data Source Reliability Notes
summary: DEA Hotspots and Open-Meteo are live inputs; Elastic MCP provides policy, playbook, and historical evidence.
content: DEA Hotspots and Open-Meteo weather are live operational inputs in this demo. Official warning coverage may vary by state. Spatial exposure can fall back to seeded demo data if the live provider times out. Elastic MCP is used for searchable operational memory, policy documents, playbooks, templates, and historical incident evidence rather than raw live weather or hotspot collection.
